overview: This House resolution set the rules for the House's final vote on H.R. 1, the large budget reconciliation bill, after the Senate had passed its own changed version. Reconciliation is a special budget process that lets certain tax and spending bills pass the Senate with a simple majority. The resolution allowed a motion for the House to accept the Senate's version as-is, set aside procedural objections, and limited debate to one hour split between the leaders of the Budget and Ways and Means committees. Accepting the Senate version meant the bill could go straight to the President. The House adopted the resolution on July 3, 2025.
for: Supporters say it let the House finish a major bill quickly by accepting the Senate's version, avoiding further back-and-forth between the chambers.
against: Critics say one hour of debate with no chance to offer changes was far too little for a bill of that size and impact.
